```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`new_chart_block()` draws the data it receives as an interactive chart and
passes the data on, filtered by the reader's last click if `drill` is set.
Everything below can also be set in the block's gear; the gear and the code
write the same arguments.

Run any of these with a data frame of your own:

```{r}
library(blockr.core)
library(blockr.viz)

serve(
  new_chart_block(type = "bar", category = "Species",
                  value = "Sepal.Length", func = "mean"),
  data = list(data = iris)
)
```

## Types

| type | draws | set |
|---|---|---|
| `"bar"`, `"waterfall"`, `"pie"`, `"treemap"` | one mark per category, aggregated | `category`, `value`, `func` |
| `"boxplot"`, `"pointrange"` | the spread of a column per category | `category`, `value`, `summary` |
| `"histogram"` | the rows of one numeric column, binned | `x`, `bins` |
| `"scatter"`, `"line"`, `"area"` | one mark per row | `x`, `y` |
| `"band"` | a running quantile band across individuals | `x`, `y`, `id` |
| `"gantt"` | intervals on lanes | `x`, `xend`, `y` |

## Category and value

An aggregated type draws one mark per value of `category`, and aggregates
`value` with `func`. A row count needs no `value`. `orientation` turns the
marks and changes nothing else:

```{r}
# counts per class, horizontal bars
new_chart_block(type = "bar", category = "class")

# counts per class, vertical bars
new_chart_block(type = "bar", category = "class", orientation = "vertical")

# summed sales per region
new_chart_block(type = "bar", category = "region", value = "sales",
                func = "sum")
```

`x` and `y` are for the types that draw one mark per row (scatter, line,
area, band), the histogram and the gantt.

`func` is one of `"count"`, `"count_distinct"`, `"pct_distinct"`,
`"mean"`, `"median"`, `"sum"`, `"min"`, `"max"` or `"identity"` (the value
as it is).

## Splitting the marks

`color` colors, `series` splits rows into lines or point groups, `facet`
draws one panel per level, and `label` writes a column on the marks.

```{r}
new_chart_block(type = "bar", category = "class", value = "hwy",
                func = "mean", color = "drv", position = "dodge")

new_chart_block(type = "line", x = "date", y = "value", color = "country",
                facet = "region", facet_cols = 3, legend = "marks")
```

`position` is `"stack"`, `"dodge"` or `"fill"` (shares of 100 percent).
`legend` is `"bottom"`, `"top"`, `"marks"` (names at the end of the lines or
on the slices) or `"none"`. `highlight` keeps a few marks in color and grays
the rest:

```{r}
new_chart_block(type = "line", x = "year", y = "gdp", color = "country",
                highlight = list(country = "Switzerland"))
```

## Lines, bands and ranges

```{r}
# a forecast fan: nested bands, the first the outermost
new_chart_block(type = "line", x = "date", y = "fc",
                ymin = c("lo95", "lo80"), ymax = c("hi95", "hi80"))

# a target line and a shaded period
new_chart_block(type = "line", x = "date", y = "rate",
                value_lines = c(Target = 2),
                x_ranges = list(Recession = c("2008-01-01", "2009-06-30")))

# a scatter with a linear trend per group, on a log axis
new_chart_block(type = "scatter", x = "gdp", y = "life", color = "continent",
                smoother = "lm", x_transform = "log10")
```

## Numbers

`format` prints the values on the axis, in tooltips and in value labels:
`"number"`, `"compact"` (1.2K), `"percent"`, or a number of decimals from 0
to 6. `unit` is text after the number.

```{r}
new_chart_block(type = "bar", category = "region", value = "share",
                func = "mean", format = "percent", value_labels = TRUE)
```

## Titles

`title`, `subtitle` and `caption` take templates. `{@arg}` prints one of the
block's own settings, and the reader can change it by clicking it on the
chart. A part in `[...]` disappears when it would be empty.

```{r}
new_chart_block(
  type = "bar", category = "class", value = "hwy", func = "mean",
  title = "Highway mileage by class",
  subtitle = "{@func in mean, median} of {label(@value)}[ by {@color}]"
)
```

## Clicks

With `drill`, a click filters the block's output to the rows behind the
clicked mark: set it to a column, or to `"auto"` for the mark's own
category. Blocks linked below the chart then show only those rows. A brush
on a scatter or a line filters to the brushed range.

```{r}
new_chart_block(type = "bar", category = "region", drill = "auto")
```

## Downloads

With `download = TRUE` (the default) the block offers Excel (the rows),
an image, a web page and PowerPoint (the chart as drawn).
